name: ateam-security-audit
description: Audit, fix, verify, repeat. A security audit loop for software projects: open-source scanners for secrets, code, dependencies, infrastructure and CI, plus the agent's own review of access control, business logic and AI features. Findings go into a tracked register, developers fix them, rescans confirm every fix, and a gate decides when the project is ready for sign-off.

interface.longDescription:
Security Audit Loop runs a full security audit of a software project and keeps the team on it until every blocking issue is fixed and confirmed.

It runs free, open-source scanners (Gitleaks, Semgrep Community Edition, OSV-Scanner, Checkov and zizmor) where they're installed, adds its own review of access control, business logic and AI features, and writes every finding to a register in the project, with a permanent ID, severity, OWASP and CWE mapping, and an owner. Developers fix findings one at a time and, for serious ones, state the root cause. A rescan confirms each fix before it's closed, and a gate decides when the project is ready for sign-off.

Three skills: security-audit (scope, scan and register), security-fix (root cause, fix, variants, secret rotation, false positives and accepted risks) and security-verify (rescan, gate, sign-off report and CI setup).

Instructions only: no servers, hooks or scripts. Scanners run on your machine with your approval, and the skills tell the agent to mask secret values. A passed gate means no blocking findings remained against the stated scope; it isn't a guarantee that the application is secure.
